title: Tight Bounds for Sorting Under Partial Information
authors: Ivor van der Hoog (Technical University of Denmark, Denmark), Daniel Rutschmann (Technical University of Denmark, Denmark)
abstract:
Sorting is one of the fundamental algorithmic problems in theoretical computer science. It has a natural generalization, introduced by Fredman in 1976, called sorting under partial information. The input consists of: - a ground set X of size n, - a partial oracle P (where partial oracle queries for any (xi, xj) output whether xi

= 1, our algorithm can preprocess P using O(n^(1 + 1/c)) partial oracle queries and time. Given L, we uncover the linear order on X using θ(c \log e(P)) linear oracle queries and time, which is worst-case optimal. We show a matching lower bound for the prepossessing also, as we show that there exist positive constants (α, β) where for any constant c > 3, any algorithm that uses at most α n^(1 + 1/c) partial oracle queries must use worst-case at least β c log e(P) linear oracle queries. Thus, we solve the problem of sorting under partial information through an algorithm that is asymptotically tight across all three metrics.
